runs.text: Q1. What is full stack development, and which parts of an application does a full stack developer need to understand?

Full stack development means being able to work on every part of an application. Any application can be seen as made of three important components: the front end, the back end and the database. The front end is what the user sees and interacts with, the ba

ck end is the logic that processes requests behind the scenes, and the database is where the application's data is stored. A full stack developer needs a basic understanding of how all three work and how they fit together before going deep into any one tec
hnology.
Q2. What is the front end of an application?

The front end is the part of an application that the user can see and interact with. On a shopping website, for example, the images of products, the text, the colors, the links and the layout of the pag
e all belong to the front end. It is called the front end because it is presented to the user. It is built with front-end technologies, which decide what is shown on the screen and how it looks.
Q3. What is the back end of an application?
The back end is t

he part of an application that works behind the scenes. It holds the logic and does the processing that the user never sees. When the user performs an action such as a search or a click, the back end processes that request and decides what information has
to be sent back. It is written with a back-end programming language such as Java, Python or C#.
Q4. What is the difference between the front end and the back end?
- Visibility: the front end is visible to the user, while the back end is hidden from the use
r.
- Purpose: the front end presents the application (images, text, colors, links, buttons), while the back end contains the logic and processing that decide what is shown.
- Technologies: the front end is built with front-end technologies such as HTML, wh
ile the back end is built with a programming language such as Java, Python or C#.
The two work together: the front end lets the user perform an action, and the back end processes the action and returns the result that the front end displays.
Q5. On an onli
ne shopping website, a user searches for 'iPhone' and only iPhone products appear. Which part of the application is responsible for what?
The screen with its images, prices, text and links is the front end. The user types the search text and sees the resul
t there.

The work of picking only the iPhone products out of all the products, and leaving out other phones, is processing done at the back end. The user cannot see this processing; only the final result is visible.

The same happens when a user clicks a category such as Fashion or Mobiles. Only the products of that category appear because the back end processed the click and returned the matching information. The front end alone can display things, but it cannot decid
e what to show without this processing.
Q6. Which technologies are used for the front end and which for the back end?
The front end is designed with front-end technologies. The first of these to be learned is HTML, which is used to design the pages; other
front-end technologies such as CSS and JavaScript are learned along with it. HTML decides what is placed on a page, such as text, images, boxes and buttons.
The back end is written with a back-end programming language such as Java, Python or C#. The langua
ge is used to write the logic that decides what should happen when a request arrives, and which page or data has to be given back.
Q7. What are web pages, and what is HTML used for?
Every application is built from pages. A streaming application, for instan
ce, can have a home page, a sign-up page, a login page and a movies page. The number of pages depends on the requirements of the application, and each page shows its own content.
HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language. It is the technology used to desig

n these pages: the text, the boxes, the buttons and the layout that the user sees. It can also provide links from one page to other pages. When the server responds to a request, the response is an HTML page, and the browser displays it to the user.
Q8. Wha
t is a browser, and what is the World Wide Web?

A browser is a software application that is used to access websites on the internet. Examples are Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge and Safari. When a website address is typed into the browser, the browser sends
a request on behalf of the user and displays the response that comes back.
The World Wide Web (WWW) is the collection of websites and web resources that are accessed through the internet. A browser is the tool through which a user reaches the World Wide We
b.
Q9. What are the main parts of a website address?
A website address has three main parts: the protocol, the domain name and the resource.
https://www.netflix.com/login
- Protocol: the set of rules used for communication, such as http or https (written a
t the beginning of the address).
- Domain name: the name of the website, such as netflix.com.
- Resource: the particular page or item that is being requested on that website, such as the login page.
The address shown above is only an illustration of the fo
rmat. Websites such as Netflix and Facebook all follow the same standard format.
Q10. What is a domain name?
A domain name is the name by which a website is identified, such as netflix.com or facebook.com. It is the part of the address that comes after the
protocol and tells the browser which website is to be reached. Every website has a domain name, and all websites follow the same pattern of protocol, domain name and resource.
Q11. What is a resource in a website?
A resource is a specific page or piece of

content that a website provides. One website has many resources. On a streaming website, the login page, the sign-up page, the payments page and the movies pages are all separate resources, and each of them is located at its own address. The part of the a
ddress after the domain name indicates which resource is being asked for.
When the user clicks on the Sign Up option, the resource that is requested changes from the login page to the sign-up page, and the address shown in the browser changes accordingly.
Q12. What is a URL, and what does it stand for?

URL stands for Uniform Resource Locator. It is the complete address used to locate a particular resource on the web. It combines the protocol, the domain name and the resource, as in https://www.netflix.com/l
ogin. Every resource of a website has its own URL, so a URL is what the browser uses to find the exact page that is required.
Q13. What is a client in the client-server model?

A client is the computer from which a request is sent. The user's own computer or phone, with a browser opened on it, is the client. The word client is only a technical term for the machine that asks for information.
Q14. What is a server, and why is it ca
lled a big computer that runs all the time?

A server is a computer that receives requests from clients, processes them and sends back responses. The server of a company such as Netflix is a very large and powerful computer, much more capable than an ordina

ry personal computer. It is kept running twenty-four hours a day, seven days a week, so that a user can open the application and watch at any time. The company's own computers hold the application and its pages, and every client reaches them through reques
ts.
Q15. What is the request-response architecture?

In the request-response architecture, the client sends a request and the server sends back a response. When a user types a website address in the browser and presses Enter, the browser sends a request fro

m the client to the server of that website, asking for some information. The server processes the request and sends back a response, which in this case is the page that the user wants to see. When the user clicks on the Sign Up option, another request goes
to the server, and the sign-up page comes back as the response.
The request sent from the browser is called an HTTP request, and the reply from the server is called an HTTP response. Applications such as Facebook, Netflix and sports applications all follo
w this same design: a request is sent, and a response comes back.
Q16. How does the browser know which page to display, and what decides it?
The browser does not decide this on its own. For every request, the server sends back an HTML page as the response.

A website has many pages, and different requests get different pages: one request gets the home page, another gets the sign-up page. The back-end logic, written in a back-end programming language, decides which page or data is to be given for a request. T
he browser only displays what comes back in the response.
Q17. What are the differences between a web application, a desktop application and a mobile application?
- Web application: any application that needs the internet to run, such as Netflix or Faceboo
k. It is opened through a browser and works by sending requests to a server.
- Desktop (local) application: an application that runs on the local system and does not need the internet, for example MS Paint.
- Mobile application: an application that runs on
a phone, such as an Android or iOS application.
Applications of all these kinds are built in different ways, but the applications that communicate with a server follow the same request and response pattern.
